content: 1. Magnesium oxide: Administer magnesium oxide at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Magnesium oxide reduces rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor therapy closely. 2. Antacids: Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine can significantly decrease rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. If antacids must be used, administer them at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. For combination products like dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours after administration. Monitor closely. 3. Magnesium sulfate: Similar to magnesium oxide, magnesium sulfate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Monitor therapy closely. 4. Maprotiline: Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of maprotiline by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 5. Mavorixafor: Mavorixafor increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QTc closely, especially in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. 6. Mefloquine: Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of mefloquine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. 7. Methadone: No dose adjustments are required when co-administering methadone with rilpivirine. However, rilpivirine increases methadone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Mirtazapine: Both mirtazapine and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Moxifloxacin: Moxifloxacin increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, and rilpivirine increases moxifloxacin toxicity similarly. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Nelfinavir: Nelfinavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Nevirapine: Nevirapine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be used with NNRTIs due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance. 13. Nilotinib: Rilpivirine increases nilotinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Nizatidine: Nizatidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Monitor closely. 15. Nortriptyline: Rilpivirine increases nortriptyline toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Octreotide: Rilpivirine increases octreotide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ofloxacin: Rilpivirine increases ofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Olanzapine: Both olanzapine and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (Viekira Pak): This combination increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to QT interval prolongation. Co-administration is not recommended. Use an alternative drug. 20. Omeprazole: Omeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance. 21. Orlistat: Orlistat decreases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 22. Osilodrostat: Both osilodrostat and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Oxaliplatin: Both oxaliplatin and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration and use an alternative drug. 24. Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance. 25. Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance. 26. Pimozide: Rilpivirine increases pimozide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Posaconazole: Posaconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine also increases posaconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Potassium chloride: Potassium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer at least 2 hours before or after rilpivirine. Monitor closely. 29. Primaquine: Both primaquine and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Procainamide: Rilpivirine increases procainamide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Propafenone: Rilpivirine increases propafenone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Protriptyline: Rilpivirine increases protriptyline toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Quetiapine: Rilpivirine increases quetiapine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Quinidine: Rilpivirine increases quinidine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Quinine: Rilpivirine increases quinine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Quizartinib: Both quizartinib and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered. 37. Rabeprazole: Rabeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance. 38. Ranolazine: Rilpivirine increases ranolazine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Ribociclib: Ribociclib increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration and use an alternative drug. 40. Rifabutin: Rifabutin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered, increase rilpivirine dose to 50 mg once daily. When rifabutin is discontinued, reduce rilpivirine dose to 25 mg once daily. 41. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance. 42. Rifapentine: Rifapentine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance. 43. Risperidone: Rilpivirine increases risperidone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine also increases ritonavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Romidepsin: Rilpivirine increases romidepsin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Selpercatinib: Selpercatinib increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Sertraline: Both sertraline and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Sevoflurane: Both sevoflurane and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration and use an alternative drug. 49. Siponimod: Both siponimod and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration and use an alternative drug. 50. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. Monitor closely. 51. Solifenacin: Both solifenacin and rilpivirine prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Sotalol: Rilpivirine increases sotalol toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of treatment failure and resistance.
